oewn-07123904-n.learner: communication by talking out loud, using spoken words rather than writing or signs
examples: She preferred speech to writing when she had news to share.

oewn-07085523-n.learner: your own usual way or style of speaking
examples: Her speech was calm and careful, and she never raised her voice.

oewn-07023937-n.learner: the words that the characters say to each other in a play
examples: She learned her speech for the school play by heart.

oewn-05658665-n.learner: the power of the mind that lets you talk to others with your voice
examples: After the illness he lost the power of speech for a week.

oewn-06726869-n.learner: a long telling-off for something someone did wrong
examples: When I came home late, my father gave me a speech about keeping my word.

connotation.why: casts a scolding as long-winded talk

oewn-09782244-n.learner: a person who has done well many times in what they have tried
examples: Everyone in the family agreed that her uncle was a success.

oewn-01233454-n.learner: the act of people coming together for a shared purpose
examples: His meeting with the builders to plan the new house went well.

oewn-00147676-n.learner: the act of joining together to become one
examples: The talks ended in a meeting of minds, and the two sides agreed at last.

oewn-08560197-n.learner: a place where things join or flow together, most often rivers
examples: The town was built at the meeting of two rivers.
The empty street at dawn was a strange sight.

oewn-82981785-n.learner: a place that is interesting to see, especially for visitors
examples: We spent the day seeing the sights of London.

oewn-00883327-n.learner: the act of looking at, seeing, or watching something
examples: From the tower they took a long sight over the whole valley.

oewn-06220699-n.learner: what a person can see or judge in their mind; their way of seeing things
examples: In the sight of the law, all people are equal.

oewn-13796604-n.learner: a large number, amount, or size of something
examples: It cost a sight of money to mend the roof.

oewn-02291532-v.learner: to find something without expecting to
examples: While digging in the garden, she discovered an old silver coin.

oewn-02132531-v.learner: to see something for the first time, or to find something new
examples: The sailors discovered an island that was on none of their maps.

oewn-00654017-v.learner: to identify what something is, as when you work out what kind of plant or animal you have found.
examples: Using the key in her field guide, she discovered the plant to be a kind of wild orchid.

oewn-01732234-v.learner: to play music that goes along with and supports a singer or another player
examples: She sang while her sister accompanied her on the piano.

oewn-01293025-v.learner: to become joined or fixed to something
examples: The seeds attach to your socks when you walk through long grass.

oewn-02278138-v.learner: to take and hold someone's property for a time as a guarantee, using the power of the law
examples: The court attached his wages until the debt was paid.
The two ladies were delighted to see their dear friend again, called it an age since they had met.
"Yes, madam," said Mrs. Bennet, delighted to speak to a Lady Catherine.

oewn-00868825-s.learner: full of wonder and great pleasure
examples: The delighted children stared as the magician pulled a bird out of his hat.

oewn-01199335-v.learner: to eat all the food on your plate or on the table
examples: He finished everything on his plate and asked for more.

oewn-01268553-v.learner: to give the surface of something a final coat or look
examples: They finished the table with a coat of dark varnish.

oewn-00352617-v.learner: to make someone end a relationship with another person
examples: His rudeness at dinner finished her with him for good.
Only people of quality were invited to the ball.

oewn-04994869-n.learner: the special character of a sound, such as a voice, a noise, or a musical note, that makes it different from other sounds
examples: The singer's voice had a warm, soft quality.
